title: Exactness of the canonical finite residue realization
statement: For any scheme X and finite discrete topological commutative ring A, the specified integralModelIntrinsicRealization of [def-sfb-embedded-integral-model-coefficients] preserves finite limits and finite colimits. It uses the actual restriction to constant scalar functions. The helper constructions name the canonical first derived reduction and the constant-residue and intrinsic bounded-constructible cohomology predicates, with their coefficient and derived-category instances fixed.

proof.text: The constant-ring module equivalence identifies the fixed-coefficient additive forgetful functor with the additive forgetful functor following an equivalence. Hence it preserves finite limits and colimits and reflects them because it reflects isomorphisms.

The composite of fixed-scalar restriction with that forgetful functor is the original additive forgetful functor. Reflect finite limits and colimits to prove restriction exact. Compose with the exact continuous section-action equivalence and intrinsic realization. Name the induced termwise derived functor with these exactness instances; this is a construction, not a chosen existence witness.
